title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

reports.title: KAKE NEWS INVESTIGATES: Duplicate license plate numbers lead to dangerous situations for some Kansas drivers

summary:
Matthew and Leah Spurlock were repeatedly pulled over because their Kansas KU Alumni license plate number, 7007, matched a stolen GMC pickup's temporary Kansas tag. In Colwich, Kansas, a Flock camera alerted police to a possible stolen vehicle, but an officer recognized their minivan. Later, in Catoosa, Oklahoma, another Flock camera led police to stop them at gunpoint and handcuff Matthew. The plate numbers were the same, but the plate backgrounds and types were different.

Wichita police Captain Casey Slaughter said Flock cameras read only letters and numbers, not plate types. Kansas has more than 100 plate designs, about half specialty, and duplicates numbers. Alerts alone are not enough for a stop, but a wrong plate type entered into the system can lead officers to proceed. Slaughter said such mistakes are extremely rare. Kansas is moving from six digit to seven digit, non duplicated plate numbers. The Spurlocks' stolen vehicle entry has expired, so they no longer expect stops, though they want to keep their 14 year old plate.
